concepts.name: Decision Paralysis
concepts.description: A state where uncertainty or excessive choice prevents people from making decisions even when the best course of action is logically clear.

concepts.name: Choice Overload
concepts.description: The tendency for additional attractive options to make decision making more difficult and increase indecision.

concepts.name: Core Message Guidance
concepts.description: A clear, prioritized message that helps people make decisions by highlighting what matters most.

problems.name: Decision paralysis under uncertainty
problems.description: People struggle to act when uncertainty exists, even when the uncertainty should not affect the final decision.

problems.name: Choice overload
problems.description: People become less decisive when faced with multiple attractive alternatives.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.title: Irrelevant uncertainty can prevent action
insights.what_it_says: People often delay decisions when uncertainty exists, even if the uncertainty has no impact on the eventual outcome.
insights.why_it_matters: Communicators and leaders must recognize that uncertainty itself creates friction and can stop people from acting.

examples_from_source.what_happened: Students who knew they passed wanted the vacation and students who knew they failed also wanted the vacation. Students who did not know their results chose to wait instead.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: The uncertainty itself changed behavior despite not changing the preferred outcome.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: Reduce unnecessary uncertainty when asking people to make decisions.

decision_rules.condition: When people are delaying action despite clear benefits.
decision_rules.action: Clarify outcomes and remove unnecessary unknowns.
decision_rules.rationale: Uncertainty can create paralysis independent of actual consequences.

patterns.description: People postpone decisions when an unresolved uncertainty exists.

warnings.warning: Assuming uncertainty is harmless when it does not affect outcomes.
warnings.consequence: People may delay or avoid action.
warnings.prevention: Address uncertainty directly and simplify choices.

application_patterns.when_to_use: When designing products, communications, or policies that require action.
application_patterns.adaptation_notes: Useful in marketing, product design, leadership communication, and behavioral change.

when_not_to_use: Situations where uncertainty itself is essential information
tradeoffs: Reducing uncertainty increases action but may simplify complex realities.
insights.evidence: Tversky and Shafir's study shows us that uncertainty—even irrelevant uncertainty—can paralyze us.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.title: Additional choices can increase indecision
insights.what_it_says: Adding attractive alternatives can make people less likely to choose any of them, even when the alternatives are desirable.
insights.why_it_matters: More options do not always improve decisions. They can increase hesitation and reduce action.

examples_from_source.what_happened: Students were less likely to choose the attractive lecture when another attractive alternative, a foreign film, was added.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: More choices created more indecision rather than greater satisfaction.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: Reduce competing alternatives when encouraging action.

decision_rules.condition: When action is more important than exploration.
decision_rules.action: Reduce the number of attractive alternatives.
decision_rules.rationale: Too many good choices can create paralysis.

patterns.description: The addition of appealing options reduces commitment to any single option.

warnings.consequence: People may postpone decisions or default to inaction.

application_patterns.when_to_use: When people must make a decision quickly or confidently.
application_patterns.adaptation_notes: Useful in product design, sales, marketing, and leadership.

when_not_to_use: Research environments where exploration is the goal
tradeoffs: Reducing options improves action but may reduce perceived flexibility.
insights.evidence: Paralysis can also be caused by choice.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.title: Core messages reduce decision anxiety
insights.what_it_says: A clear core message helps people navigate uncertainty and competing choices by reminding them what matters most.
insights.why_it_matters: People constantly make decisions under uncertainty. A prioritized message provides a decision shortcut.

examples_from_source.what_happened: The message 'THE low-fare airline' helped an employee reject an unnecessary expense.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: The core message simplified a difficult tradeoff.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: A clear priority helps people make consistent decisions without detailed instructions.

decision_rules.rule: Use a core message as a decision filter.
decision_rules.condition: When people face uncertainty or competing priorities.
decision_rules.action: Refer decisions back to the core principle.
decision_rules.rationale: A clear priority reduces anxiety and improves consistency.

patterns.description: A central message guides choices across many situations.

warnings.warning: Failing to provide a clear priority.
warnings.consequence: People become vulnerable to indecision and inconsistency.

application_patterns.when_to_use: When teams or audiences must make repeated decisions independently.
application_patterns.adaptation_notes: Useful in leadership, strategy, operations, and product organizations.

tradeoffs: A simple core message improves action but may omit situational nuance.
insights.evidence: Core messages help people avoid bad choices by reminding them of what's important.

relationships.evidence: Understanding uncertainty-induced paralysis helps explain decision delays.
